$note: Sync stamp for the vendored KnowledgeNetwork Design System snapshot. The DS is a Claude Design project with NO native version/release and NO per-file hashes in its manifest, so this file IS the diffable version marker of what state we adopted. To check for drift: re-read the DS via /design-sync, re-hash, and compare against `tokens.files` below; to adopt a change, re-vendor and update the hashes + syncedAt here. Graduating to a properly published/semver'd dependency is tracked in issue #66.

tokens.note: Token files are mostly verbatim copies but one has diverged. Hashes below are the last-verified DS fingerprints; re-read the DS via /design-sync to detect further DS changes. 2026-08-05 re-sync: colors.css adopted contrast pass; 2026-08-08: typography.css adopted the 2026-08-05 DS addition (--ls-caps: 0.12em added, --ls-eyebrow aliased to it — every all-caps string in the system carries --ls-caps, a system-level rule not a per-component one). 2026-08-09 re-sync: all 7 files re-hashed and the recipe pinned down (see hashRecipe) — base/colors/elevation/fonts/motion reproduce their recorded fingerprints exactly, so they are unchanged and verbatim; typography.css is byte-identical to the DS and its NEEDS_RECOMPUTE marker is now a real hash. spacing.css keeps a LOCAL deviation, but the reason has INVERTED: the DS removed the dead --road-question-h / --road-tab-h (we converge) and corrected --road-head-h 28px -> 44px explicitly to adopt our old local value, except that value is now one revision stale — #70/#86 (2d59ac3) added the description row and grew the title, so AuthorRoad.tsx:84 headH() = HEAD_TITLE(28) + HEAD_DESC(20) + HEAD_COMBO(24) = 72px. We hold 72px; the road owns its own constants. Do NOT adopt 44 back. Re-reported on drift-log #74. 2026-08-11: --road-head-h is now DEAD in the app either way — the open card's head wraps, so AuthorRoad computes its height per card via headRows() and no source reads the token. The 44-vs-72 divergence is moot until something consumes it again. 2026-08-11 colors.css re-vendored: --border-hair 0.13 -> 0.17 and --border-rule 0.20 -> 0.25, restoring the file to byte-verbatim (every other line already matched). This was SILENT drift of the worst kind: the recorded fingerprint (89d70a85...) was the hash of our own stale copy, not of the DS file, so the mechanical check that exists precisely to catch this was vouching for the divergence. The DS flagged --border-hair; --border-rule was a second drift nobody had noticed. New fingerprint eec676c8... The hashRecipe was re-verified against base.css first, which still reproduces its recorded hash exactly. 2026-08-12 (#95 + #94), all seven re-fetched from the DS and hashed at the source — see fingerprintProvenance. Recipe proven first: 6 of the 7 local files reproduced their recorded hashes, so the tr/sha256 pipeline is sound and every mismatch below is real drift, not a machine artefact. THREE files had moved. (1) base.css was a whole revision behind: the DS replaced the single soft 8px bar with the THREE-STATE scrollbar (rest hidden / on 4px / near 7px with a wash and end arrows), driven by an assets/scrollbars.js that we did not have — a stylesheet whose states nothing could ever select. Adopted with its driver, since either half alone is inert; the diff was confined entirely to the scrollbar block, every line above it byte-identical. Its four SVG data-URI arrowheads were decoded and parsed rather than eyeballed (four 12px chevrons, stroke #c8bfaf at 1.6px). (2) elevation.css: --ring-linked 2px -> 1.5px, the softest ring thinned so correspondence reads quieter than commitment. A real visual change on every cross-pane hover. (3) fonts.css: comment-only, but it documents a LOAD-BEARING limit — JetBrains Mono ships at 400 and 500 ONLY, so a mono numeral asked for --fw-semibold or --fw-bold silently renders at 500. Weight steps on counts must be regular -> medium. Nothing in this app was relying on the heavier weights, but the constraint is now written down where a future mono numeral will meet it.
tokens.fingerprintProvenance: 2026-08-12 (#95): every hash below is now the sha256 of the DS FILE'S OWN BYTES, re-fetched via /design-sync and hashed one at a time. Before today most of them were not. They had been computed from OUR vendored copy, which makes the drift check circular: it can detect a local edit and can NEVER detect upstream movement, and it will report `verified` in exactly the case it exists to catch. That is how colors.css stayed behind for days while the check passed (see the 2026-08-11 note below), and re-running the audit properly found two more of the same: elevation.css and fonts.css had BOTH drifted while vouching for themselves. Two of the seven were already honest — spacing.css (c58475d8 reproduced from the DS bytes exactly) and, since yesterday's real comparison, colors.css. The rule from here: a fingerprint is only worth recording if it was taken from the source, never from the copy.
tokens.hashRecipe: sha256 of the file's bytes with CRLF normalized to LF. This repo has core.autocrlf=true, so the working tree is CRLF while git blobs and the DS originals are LF — hashing the working-tree file raw yields a machine-local fingerprint that will never match the DS. Verify the recipe before trusting a mismatch: `tr -d '\r' < src/tokens/base.css | sha256sum` must reproduce base.css below.

tailwindTheme.hashRecipe: same as tokens.hashRecipe — sha256 of the bytes with CRLF normalized to LF. Taken from the DS file, not from our copy
tailwindTheme.note: The DS's Tailwind v4 utility surface (#93), kept OUT of tokens.files on purpose: those seven are the token definitions the app consumes as var(--…), this is a generated @theme block that turns the same values into utility classes. Imported from src/index.css after the five definition files and before base.css. INSTALLED AS ADDITIVE: the standing warning was that it overrides Tailwind's --radius-* namespace and takes rounded-lg from 8px to 20px app-wide, but that change had ALREADY happened and nobody had noticed — spacing.css declares --radius-* on :root after `@import "tailwindcss"`, so it has been overriding Tailwind's defaults since the closure landed in #64 slice 5. Measured in the browser before and after this import: rounded-sm 10px, rounded-md 14px, rounded-lg 20px, unchanged either way. So kn-theme.css adds utilities (bg-canopy, text-ink-2, shadow-lift-1, text-body, font-display, border-hair, ease-soft, the drill-* animations) and moves no pixels. Nothing in the app consumes them yet; they are there so new work stops reaching for arbitrary values. #96's Studio shell is deliberately NOT adopted alongside it — the app frame and left rail stay slate until that is decided on its own.
notVendored: export/tailwind/kn-theme.v3.js — the Tailwind v3 config form of the same theme; this app is on v4
export/tokens/kn-base.css and export/tokens/kn-tokens.css — the single-file bundles of what src/tokens/*.css already carries file-by-file

assets.note: DS material carried as-is rather than ported, so a re-sync is a copy and never a re-typing. scrollbars.js required allowJs in tsconfig.app.json for the same reason — porting it to .tsx would have made every future sync a manual merge.

src/ds/assets/leaf-mask.png.note: the leaf at half scale, alpha-only, authored by the DS expressly to fit get_file's 256 KiB cap. The full-size assets/leaf.png (1870x841) cannot cross the channel. Consumed by src/ds/chrome/LeafMark.tsx as a mask.

src/ds/assets/scrollbars.js.note: the three-state scrollbar driver (#94). Byte-verbatim; it only sets data-sb, every pixel of the three states lives in tokens/base.css, so the two are one adoption and neither works alone. Imported for its side effect from src/main.tsx after index.css, matching the DS's own delivery note. CONSEQUENCE: it publishes window.PKT_SB = { FLASH, LEAVE, PAD }, which until now did not exist in this app — PaneHeader.tsx:37, NodeChip.tsx:50 and VersionedGroup.tsx:236/361 each read PKT_SB.LEAVE and fell back to a hard-coded 500. The DS ships LEAVE: 500, so no timing changes, but those four sites are now on the DS clock for real and the 'this app has no PKT_SB' deviation recorded against PaneHeader and VersionedGroup is retired.

2026-08-12: CONSUMED at last, on the road's CLOSED container cards (#91). A shut card hosts the whole component folded — the children-are-board-level-siblings wall only binds when there are visible children, and a fold has none. The road hands over the drawing and keeps the behaviour: the wrapper owns position, the relayout transition, drag, selection, hover-dim and double-click-to-open; the component owns the picture, the title, the tally, and the two controls (its RestoreMark maximises, its ✕ ungroups — askUngroup already implements the road's refuse-when-multiple-versions rule exactly). Hosted with narrow + width=NODEW + movable=false + resizable=false, so it is TOLD its box and never measures itself, which is what lets layoutRoad place it. The OPEN card still mirrors the head by hand, so this port is now half-consumed and checkStyle stays exported
